Just four years ago, Republican Jack Ciattarelli almost won a stunning upset over Governor Phil Murphy, losing by just 3.22% despite running in a blue state. New Jersey has a long history of voting against the party in power in the White House, most recently voting for Republican Chris Christie twice even as President Obama won the state by double digits. That likely played a role in Ciattarelli’s strong showing in 2021 when Joe Biden was President, but those very same headwinds may work against him now that Donald Trump is President. Ciattarelli faces Democratic Congresswoman Mikie Sherrill, who proved to also be a strong candidate when she flipped a long-held Republican seat in 2018, winning the race by almost 15%.
